messages:
Nora C: opened a PR to tidy Dedicated provisioning docs: unify cooldown units, add Go SDK + Terraform migration example, clarify SLA wording and isolation decorators. PR: https://git.redwood/docs/pull/948
Jon S: quick skim. please make explicit difference between `tenant_labels` and `isolation_decorators` (they live in different layers: reservation vs cluster scheduling). add a short example for both.
Priya M: also call out the behavioral difference for `preemption_behavior: graceful` vs `best_effort`  graceful drains connections for up to 60s, best_effort evicts immediately. ops wants to avoid customers assuming graceful is unlimited.
DevRel Sam: I'll add a small sample repo that demonstrates tenant-label routing + fallback to hosted model (will paste link in PR). prefer adding a Go SDK example instead of Python for variety.
Nora C: adding proposed YAML snippet and a Go SDK snippet. asking for review on wording for SLA and migration commands.
```yaml
# minimal reservation + scale policy
reservation:
  name: recs-prod
  gpus: 8
  tenant_labels:
    - team:recs
  isolation_decorators:
    - no-shared-alloc
scalePolicy:
  mode: target_utilization
  target_utilization: 0.65
  cooldown_sec: 180
  preemption_behavior: graceful
```

```go
// Go SDK example (v0.7)
ctx := context.Background()
client := redwood.NewDedicatedClient()
res, err := client.CreateReservation(ctx, redwood.Reservation{
  Name:         "recs-prod",
  GPUs:         8,
  TenantLabels: []string{"team:recs"},
  IsolationDecorators: []string{"no-shared-alloc"},
})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
_, err = res.UpdateScalePolicy(ctx, redwood.ScalePolicy{
  Mode:               "target_utilization",
  TargetUtilization:  0.65,
  CooldownSec:        180,
  PreemptionBehavior: "graceful",
})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
```

Nora C: migration note suggested for Terraform/CLI users: legacy `scale_schema v1` used `cooldown` and `batch_target`. For a mass update: `sed -i 's/\bcooldown\b/cooldown_sec/g; s/\bbatch_target\b//g' **/*.tf` (test in a branch first).
ops-oncall: ops clarifications: fallback routing -> service will attempt to route to a compatible hosted model variant for up to 90s while backfill/placement completes; after that requests will return capacity errors. quota enforcement/backfill window is 15m. also note: `no-shared-alloc` decorator prevents bin-packing with other tenants but does not guarantee exclusive GPU for preemption-proof workloads.
legal: the phrase "best effort" in the SLA is ambiguous. propose: "Reserved capacity SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime for active reservations. Capacity may be preempted only for critical safety or emergency maintenance; scheduled maintenance will provide 24 hours' notice." Tagging legal reviewers for signoff.
docs-bot: link-checker: anchor `#isolation-decorators` in dedicated.md returns 404. failing link list: - https://git.redwood/docs/blob/main/dedicated.md#isolation-decorators
Jon S: small copy nit: prefer snake_case in YAML examples (`isolation_decorators`, `tenant_labels`) and keep field ordering consistent with API types.
Priya M: can we add a one-sentence compatibility tip: "If you previously relied on v1 behavior where `batch_target` implicitly limited concurrency, switch to explicit `concurrency_limit` in v2."
Nora C: action items I'm taking: 1) add the YAML + Go snippet (done here), 2) add Terraform `sed` migration example, 3) add ops fallback note and backfill window, 4) replace SLA phrasing with legal's suggestion and request review, 5) fix the broken anchor or add the isolation-decorators section. will push updates to PR and request reviews from @Jon S, @Priya M, @legal. ETA: EOD today.
DevRel Sam: I'll attach the sample repo link to the PR (demo of tenant-labels -> fallback) tomorrow morning.
ops-oncall: +1; will update internal runbook after docs merge.
Jon S: once legal signs off, please squash and merge; request a follow-up changelog entry for the CLI/terraform migration.
